prayerExcerpt.en-US: Remember also, O Lord, Thy servants and handmaids, who are gone before us with the sign of faith, and rest in the sleep of peace.

cards.excerptSource: content/do/web/www/missa/English/Ordo/Ordo.txt and Portugues/Ordo/Ordo.txt, # Canon, Commemoration of the Dead: its first sentence (the 'N. and N.' dropped, lines joined; verbatim otherwise, the pt-BR without a comma before 'Senhor' as in the source)
cards.subject: The Memento of the dead in the Canon, after the Consecration, at a Low Mass in a small old stone church, seen from a side aisle. In the foreground, half-length and in profile, a widow in a black veil and her young son kneel at the end of a pew beside a wrought-iron stand of small burning votive candles, under a plain stone cross set into the wall. Beyond them and the altar rail, the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the middle of the high altar facing it, seen from behind at an angle, his hands joined before him at the height of his chin (never above his head), his eyes fixed on the white Host lying on the corporal before him beside the chalice covered with its pall; a server kneels on the step. It is a high altar with gradines: two of the six candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal. Through a small clear side window, the crosses of the churchyard in grey morning light. Quiet, tender, hopeful. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: At the Memento of the dead the priest, 'extensis et junctis manibus ante pectus, et usque ad faciem elevatis, et intentis oculis ad Sacramentum super Altare, facit commemorationem Fidelium defunctorum' (Ritus servandus IX.2). The votive candles, the wall cross and the churchyard are the painter's setting, not a rubric.

cards.excerptSource: content/do/web/www/missa/English/Ordo/Ordo.txt and Portugues/Ordo/Ordo.txt, # Canon: the opening of Nobis quoque peccatoribus (cut before the list of saints, at a comma or colon made a full stop, lines joined; verbatim otherwise)
cards.subject: The Nobis quoque peccatoribus in the Canon of a Sunday Mass, seen from the gospel side of the sanctuary, in profile. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands upright at the middle of the high altar facing it, his head a little bowed, and strikes his breast with his right hand, his left hand resting on the white corporal, where the consecrated Host lies beside the golden chalice covered with its pall. Behind and above the altar, beyond the gradine with its tall lit candles, crucifix and white-veiled tabernacle, rises a gilded reredos painted on a gold ground with a row of holy martyrs, men and women, in white and red robes, each holding a green palm branch; no names, no lettering. On the lowest step a server in cassock and surplice kneels and strikes his own breast. Candlelight on the gold. Humble, hopeful. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: At Nobis quoque peccatoribus the priest 'vocem aliquantulum elevat et dextera manu pectus sibi percutit, sinistra posita super Corporale' (Ritus servandus IX.3). The reredos of martyrs with palms stands for the 'holy Apostles and Martyrs' the prayer goes on to name; it is decoration, like the angels of the Sanctus card.

cards.excerptSource: content/do/web/www/missa/English/Ordo/Ordo.txt and Portugues/Ordo/Ordo.txt, # Preparation for Communion: the opening of Libera nos (cut at a semicolon made a full stop; verbatim otherwise)
cards.subject: The Libera nos after the Lord's Prayer at a Sunday Mass, seen close from the epistle side of the altar and a little above it, in profile. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the middle of the high altar facing it and signs himself with the golden paten: he holds the empty paten upright in his right hand and touches it to his forehead, his left hand laid below his breast, his eyes lowered. On the white corporal before him lie the consecrated white Host and the golden chalice covered with its pall, a folded white purificator beside them; the Missal on its stand beyond, its pages showing no letters; the tall lit candles, the crucifix and the white-veiled tabernacle on the gradine. Beyond the altar rail, soft and far, the faithful kneel. Warm light on the gold of the paten. Peaceful, trusting. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After the Pater noster the priest wipes the paten and holds it upright on the altar while he says Libera nos; before 'Da propitius pacem' he 'elevat manu dextera Patenam de Altari, et seipsum cum ea signat signo crucis … Cum signat se, manum sinistram ponit infra pectus; deinde Patenam ipsam osculatur', and slips it under the Host (Ritus servandus X.1–2). The breaking of the Host and the commingling that end this prayer are in the Agnus Dei and the Fraction card.

cards.excerptSource: content/do/web/www/missa/English/Ordo/Ordo.txt and Portugues/Ordo/Ordo.txt, # Preparation for Communion: Domine, non sum dignus, said three times (once; verbatim in both languages)
cards.subject: The Domine, non sum dignus before the priest's Communion at a Sunday Mass, seen from the epistle side of the sanctuary, from a little behind the priest, at the level of the altar. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the middle of the high altar facing it, bowing a little, and strikes his breast with his right hand; in his left hand, held before him above the altar, he holds the two halves of the white Host between thumb and forefinger over the golden paten. The golden chalice stands on the white corporal covered with its pall; the tall lit candles, the crucifix and the white-veiled tabernacle on the gradine. On the lowest step a server in cassock and surplice kneels, bowed low. Beyond the altar rail the faithful kneel in the pews with bowed heads, some striking their breasts, the women veiled. Soft golden light. Humble, awed. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: The priest takes both parts of the Host in his left hand with the paten beneath, 'inter pectus et Calicem, parum inclinatus, dextera tribus vicibus percutit pectus suum, interim etiam tribus vicibus dicens voce aliquantulum elevata: Domine, non sum dignus' (Ritus servandus X.4; Fortescue, l. 5166–5174). No bell is drawn: the Missal gives none here, though custom is tolerated (Fortescue, l. 6416–6418 and note).

prayerExcerpt.en-US: Grant, O Lord, that what we have taken with our mouth, we may receive with a pure mind; and from a temporal gift may it become to us an eternal remedy.

cards.excerptSource: content/do/web/www/missa/English/Ordo/Ordo.txt and Portugues/Ordo/Ordo.txt, after the Communion: Quod ore sumpsimus (whole, lines joined; verbatim in both languages)
cards.subject: The ablutions after Communion at a Low Mass, seen close from the gospel side, looking across the altar toward the epistle corner. At the epistle side the priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands in profile, turned toward the server, holding the golden chalice in both hands above the altar's edge, the joined thumbs and forefingers of both hands held over its cup. A server in black cassock and white surplice, standing on the step below, pours water from a small glass cruet over the priest's fingers into the chalice, the cruet of red wine in his other hand. On the altar a folded white purificator and, at the middle, the corporal with the golden paten and the white pall laid on it; the lit candles and the crucifix on the gradine, the white-veiled tabernacle. Beyond the altar rail, soft and far, the faithful who have received kneel in thanksgiving, faces bowed over joined hands. Bright quiet morning light. Careful, grateful. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After receiving the Precious Blood the priest says Quod ore sumpsimus and holds out the chalice to the server at the epistle corner, 'quo vinum fundente, se purificat: deinde vino et aqua abluit pollices et indices super Calicem, quos abstergit Purificatorio, interim dicens: Corpus tuum, Domine, quod sumpsi' (Ritus servandus X.5; Fortescue, l. 5352–5362). The card shows the second ablution, over the fingers.

cards.excerptSource: content/do/web/www/missa/English/Ordo/Ordo.txt and Portugues/Ordo/Ordo.txt, # Conclusion: the opening of Placeat tibi (cut at a colon or comma made a full stop; verbatim otherwise)
cards.subject: The Placeat tibi at the end of a Sunday Mass, seen from the central aisle of the nave a few pews back, straight toward the altar. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the middle of the high altar facing it, seen from behind, his head bowed, his joined hands resting on the altar's edge. Before him at the middle of the altar the chalice stands covered with its white veil and burse; the Missal lies closed on its stand at the epistle corner. It is a high altar with gradines: six tall candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal. Two servers in cassock and surplice kneel on the lowest step. In the foreground the congregation kneels in the pews on either side of the aisle, seen from behind, heads lifted, waiting for the blessing, the women veiled. Late-morning light. Everything accomplished; a last quiet prayer. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After Ite, missa est the priest, 'ante medium Altaris stans junctis manibus super eo, et capite inclinato, dicit secreto: Placeat tibi, sancta Trinitas', then kisses the altar and blesses the people (Ritus servandus XII.1); the Missal was closed after the Postcommunion (XI.1) and the chalice stands veiled at the middle (X.5). In the old rite the dismissal comes before this prayer and the blessing.

cards.excerptSource: content/do/web/www/missa/English/Ordo/Prayers.txt and Portugues/Ordo/Prayers.txt [Ultima Evangelium], John 1:1 (its first sentence; verbatim in both languages)
cards.subject: The Last Gospel at the end of a Low Mass, seen from the nave on the gospel side, looking up at the altar at an angle. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, stands at the gospel corner of the high altar, turned toward the gospel-side altar card that leans against the gradine, seen in profile, his hands joined before his breast, reading; the card's print is too small to read. At the middle of the altar the chalice under its white veil and burse; the closed Missal on its stand at the epistle corner. It is a high altar with gradines: two of the six candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal. On the floor at the epistle side a server in black cassock and white surplice stands with joined hands. In the foreground, beyond the altar rail, the faithful stand in the pews, half-length and seen from behind, a mother in a lace veil holding a small child, an old man leaning on his cane. A clear shaft of daylight falls from a high window across the altar. Bright, final, at peace. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After the blessing the priest goes to the gospel corner, signs the altar or the book and himself, and 'junctis manibus legit Evangelium: In principio'; at Et Verbum caro factum est he genuflects, and the server 'stans a parte Epistolae' answers Deo gratias (Ritus servandus XII.1). The Last Gospel stands on the gospel-side altar card (Fortescue, l. 2988–2989); all stand for it (l. 6697). The card shows the reading, not the genuflection, which would repeat the Profession of Faith card.

cards.excerptSource: content/do/web/www/missa/English/Ordo/Ordo.txt and Portugues/Ordo/Ordo.txt, # Leonine Prayers / # Oratio Leonis XIII: the opening of the prayer to St. Michael (verbatim in both languages; pt-BR keeps the source's European spelling 'demónio')
cards.subject: The prayers after Low Mass, seen from the central aisle of the nave, straight toward the altar. The priest, in a white-and-gold Roman fiddleback chasuble with the maniple on his left arm, over an amice and a lace-trimmed alb, kneels on the lowest altar step at the middle, facing the altar, seen from behind, his hands joined, a small prayer card propped against the step before him; beside him at the epistle side a server in black cassock and white surplice kneels. Above them rises a high altar with gradines: two of the six candles lit on the gradine, a central crucifix, three altar cards, and the tabernacle veiled in white silk; a white frontal; the chalice stands under its white veil and burse at the middle. At the left, in a side niche, a statue of Our Lady crowned, holding the Child, with flowers and a small blue lamp before it; high in a stained-glass window at the right, St. Michael the Archangel in golden armour with a raised sword, a dark dragon under his feet. In the foreground the congregation kneels in the pews, seen from behind, praying together, rosaries in their hands, the women veiled. Gentle morning light. Earnest, united. Keep everything inside the pointed arch. The card's frame is exactly the attached cards': the coloured initial box at the top-left, one vine-and-flower band to its right along the top and one along the bottom, plain parchment margins down the sides, and the arched window ending ABOVE the bottom band.
cards.frame: the inner window is a POINTED GOTHIC ARCH with slender gold tracery at its tip, like a sanctuary seen through a church arch; no halo
cards.basis: After every Low Mass the celebrant says with the people the prayers prescribed by Leo XIII in 1884 and 1886: 'he kneels on the lowest step and either says them from memory or reads them from a card provided' (Fortescue, l. 5479–5486); the card stands against the lowest step at the epistle side (l. 2995–2997) and the server kneels there (l. 6540–6543). The Ordo gives three Hail Marys, the Hail Holy Queen, the prayer for the Church and the prayer to St. Michael, hence the statue of Our Lady and the St. Michael window, which are decoration.
